result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers open by calling the set coherent, but then list a long run of additions, which works against the rubric's few-changes, keep-it-short goal. B is somewhat better. It praises the existing design specifically, says up front that its contrast figures are estimates to verify, and ties additions such as touch targets to the warehouse use case. A states the border contrast failures as fact and piles on more speculative tokens (z-index, breakpoints, extra spacing steps, more easings, surface tiers). | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers open by calling the set coherent, but both then suggest far more additions than a sanity pass needs. A is a bit leaner, ties most additions to real warehouse needs (control borders, focus, touch targets, tabular numbers), and treats contrast figures as estimates to verify. B adds more speculative tokens (z-index, breakpoints, extra easings, more spacing steps, a mono font, hover-row colors) and states the border's WCAG failure as fact before hedging later.
